help_topics.title: Understanding permissions and personal configuration
help_topics.business_question: Can this help show another user’s effective work configuration?
help_topics.plain_answer: This help library explains general work-selection rules. It does not access individual users, permissions or effective profiles. A colleague’s settings cannot be inferred from configuration totals or from the parameters a procedure accepts.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Work selection accepts a user and warehouse and applies profile and sequence rules.
The retained configuration checks aggregate fixed fields. They do not identify the profile applied to an individual operator.

configuration_dependencies: User, warehouse, profile, sequence and feature settings can change the work-selection path.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: For an individual access problem, use an authorized, sanitized explanation of the relevant permission/profile and application binding; do not provide another person’s operational data.
boundaries: No user-specific permission decision or access-control result is established by this prototype.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Why can’t aggregate profile totals tell me which rules a colleague uses?
must_explain: Explain the distinction between general rules, aggregate evidence and a specific user.
must_not_claim: Disclose or guess a colleague profile or permission.

help_topics.title: Handling missing locating settings
help_topics.business_question: What happens if a locating setting is missing?
help_topics.plain_answer: A missing setting does not have one universal SCALE fallback. First identify the exact locating rule, item or rule-set assignment, applicable preference and application path. The documented delayed-locating behavior requires both flags; absence of evidence is not permission to invent an active value.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Locating selects a storage destination through a rule and strategy.
Check the documented assignment and the exact setting’s fallback before predicting the result. The current introductory passage does not establish every missing-row branch.

configuration_dependencies: Item versus rule-set assignment and the two delayed-locating flags affect the documented path.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Obtain a sanitized rule identifier, setting name and application-to-rule binding. Inspect the matching documented or source-defined missing-value branch.
boundaries: No general first-match, enabled or disabled default is inferred for an absent setting.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Does an absent locating flag automatically mean delayed locating is enabled?
must_explain: Explain the two-flag dependency and unresolved specific missing-setting behavior.
must_not_claim: Assume that a missing value enables locating.

help_topics.title: Understanding duplicate or overlapping configuration
help_topics.business_question: Two profile or rule rows seem to apply. Which one wins?
help_topics.plain_answer: The winner depends on the exact query or application rule. In the reviewed work selector, some options use profile alone and others also use sequence. Do not assume that the first displayed row wins or that a primary key on an unrelated field makes the selection unique.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Identify the statement and its actual profile, sequence, warehouse and user filters.
Inspect its ordering, uniqueness constraints and fallback. Where no unique ordering is established, retain the selection ambiguity.

configuration_dependencies: Changing sequence scope can change which rows qualify. Different routines can use different precedence.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Compare only the needed sanitized keys and the applicable rule’s ordering; do not execute the work selector as a read-only diagnostic because a branch changes instruction sequence.
boundaries: This explains an ambiguity to check; it does not establish that duplicate rows exist here.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Does the first row shown on a configuration screen always take precedence?
must_explain: Explain exact-query scope, ordering and possible ties.

help_topics.title: Current documentation baseline and retained configuration checks
help_topics.business_question: Do the retained checks prove today’s effective settings?
help_topics.plain_answer: The owner confirms the replica is current and accepts it as the documentation baseline. The five retained configuration checks still describe aggregate fields observed on 29 September 2026 at 22:50:28–30 UTC; they do not identify an individual user’s effective preference or prove a specific runtime outcome.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Keep the capture time and fixed check scope attached to the result.
For a specific user or action, identify the effective setting scope. Current replica status does not turn aggregate counts into individual configuration values.

configuration_dependencies: Profile assignment and sequence precedence determine which configuration applies; aggregate checks do not expose those per-user values.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Use the named setting, screen and applicable preference/profile to explain the question. Version/build and replica synchronization evidence are not prerequisites for this documentation task.
boundaries: Current replica status is owner-attested. The retained checks are timestamped aggregate observations, not a live per-user configuration lookup.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Can yesterday’s configuration snapshot guarantee my setting now?
must_explain: State owner-attested current baseline, retained timestamp and aggregate-versus-user scope.
must_not_claim: Guarantee current primary or per-user settings.

help_topics.title: Using LAND and other product-specific SDDs
help_topics.business_question: Can the LAND SDD supply our SCALE settings?
help_topics.plain_answer: LAND describes Manhattan Active Warehouse Management (MAWM). Keep it as comparison material. Its configuration choices do not become SCALE defaults merely because both products use Manhattan names or the files share a folder.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: The document body names Manhattan Active Warehouse Management.
Its revision history ends at 2.11 dated 29 April 2025. That identifies this design revision, not a SCALE product release.
Any proposed cross-product behavior needs separate product- and version-specific applicability evidence.

configuration_dependencies: Product, release, implementation choices and document revision are separate dimensions.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Use a SCALE-specific source for a SCALE setting. Record a proposed shared claim and its exact supporting product/version evidence before applying it.
boundaries: No SCALE configuration recommendation or deployment behavior is derived from LAND. Only this reviewed claim is available in the local prototype; the raw SDD corpus remains outside production search.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Does MAWM revision 2.11 establish a SCALE release or default?
must_explain: Identify MAWM and separate document revision from product release.

help_topics.title: Explaining conflicting cycle-count tolerances
help_topics.business_question: Is our cycle-count tolerance zero or 9999?
help_topics.plain_answer: These documents do not establish our active tolerance. The Grupo Julio SDD reports a then-current value of 9999 and describes a planned zero tolerance. The Covetrus design separately specifies zero by default and leaves a note about revisiting positive tolerances. These are implementation choices with unresolved context, not a universal SCALE default.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Cycle counting compares physical and recorded stock; tolerance and approval rules influence discrepancy handling.
Read Grupo’s current-versus-intended statements together across pages 94–95.
Keep Covetrus’s default and later note attached to that implementation instead of selecting one document value for this deployment.

configuration_dependencies: Tolerance units, scope and recount/reconciliation permissions must be established for the actual deployment.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Obtain a sanitized installed tolerance definition, units, scope, approval behavior and observation date. Neither sample design establishes those current facts.
boundaries: The word current belongs to the source document’s account; it does not describe this assessed database today.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Should I copy 9999 from Grupo or zero from Covetrus?
must_explain: Explain source-specific current/planned/default values and missing deployment evidence.
must_not_claim: Select either number as the active setting.

help_topics.title: Understanding wave duration and statement timing
help_topics.business_question: How long does an entire wave take?
help_topics.plain_answer: The retained Query Store evidence cannot answer the whole-wave duration. It contains statement statistics for 163 historical object IDs. A statement can execute several times inside a procedure, and a wave can include application, queue, database and external stages. Statement counts are not procedure-call counts.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Keep object, replica group, execution type and retained interval dimensions with statement statistics.
A weighted mean combines recorded statement executions; it is not a start-to-finish wave time or a sum of all application stages.
A process measurement requires correlated start/end events, stage boundaries, retries and completion acknowledgment across the involved components.

configuration_dependencies: Queue delay, configuration choices, asynchronous work, retries and external completion can fall outside SQL statement measurements.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Use a sanitized event-schema example with correlation ID and UTC stage start/end semantics, plus observation time and process scope. Do not execute warehouse work to manufacture a timing result.
boundaries: Current object-name matches do not establish the historical definition used by Query Store. Missing history does not prove a routine is unused. No continuous interval coverage is assumed.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Can I add SQL statement averages to get the full wave time?
must_explain: Separate weighted statement averages from correlated process duration.
must_not_claim: Report Query Store counts as calls or complete elapsed time.

help_topics.title: Checking label prerequisites before assuming print success
help_topics.business_question: Does selecting a document prove the label printed?
help_topics.plain_answer: No. The SCALE 2021 training deck lists a label file, sometimes a stored procedure, document type, document and routing configuration, an optional wave label step, and a 203-dpi-compatible printer. Choosing a document, dispatching it and receiving physical output are different stages.
help_topics.trigger: A request to understand the evidence and applicability of a SCALE explanation.
input_context: The named setting or process, relevant warehouse/profile scope and observation date.

execution_steps.explanation: Check the cited template and configuration dependencies documented for the label.
When printing during a wave, the deck includes a Documents–Labels step.
Installed printer support and actual output need their own evidence; a returned document choice is not that evidence.

configuration_dependencies: Template, renderer, routing, wave step and printer support depend on the configured printing path.
expected_results: A bounded explanation and the smallest evidence needed to resolve remaining uncertainty.
explanation_paths: Use a sanitized installed template/renderer mapping and acknowledgment contract. No label, report or print job is executed by this help.
boundaries: The 203-dpi statement is this training source’s requirement, not a verified inventory of installed printers or support in every SCALE release.
No operational records, user profiles, procedures, jobs or printer outputs were requested or executed.

cases.question: Does the training deck prove our installed printer supports this label?
must_explain: Explain documented prerequisites and missing installed/output evidence.
must_not_claim: Claim verified printer support or physical output.
